Theme

Latin word

gestiō

gestiō, gestīre

verb, fourth conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

be itching to; be excited, be beside oneself with joy; be itching to; be itching to, be dying to

In this lexicon

  • be itching to

    the recommended word · classical · Traupman 101, 155; Cic.; Traupman 101: gestiō quidem (+ inf.); Traupman 335

  • excited

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. Eun. 558: Chaerea, quid est quod sīc gestīs?; Cic. Fin. 2.14 (Lewis & Short): quōrum alter laetitiā gestiat, alter dolōre cruciētur

  • look forward to

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.11.1: gestiō scīre ista omnia; Hor. Ars 159: gestit paribus conlūdere

Examples

  • «Gestiō gustāre!» «Post cēnam gustābimus.»

    “I’m itching to taste it!” “We’ll taste it after dinner.”Libellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

    In the entry for be itching to

  • Quid agās, valdē aveō scīre.

    I’m dying to know how you are doing.Cic. Att. 1.15 (Lewis & Short s.v. aveō: valdē aveō scīre quid agās); Traupman 337

    In the entry for be itching to

  • Chaerea, quid est quod sīc gestīs? quid sibi hic vestītus quaerit? Quid est quod laetus sīs?

    Chaerea, why are you so excited? What’s the meaning of these clothes? What are you so happy about?Ter. Eun. 558–559

    In the entry for excited

  • ut aliquid scīre sē gaudeant? ut id aliīs narrāre gestiant?

    how glad they are to know something, and how they long to tell it to others?Cic. Fin. 5.48

    In the entry for excited
